question: Two hemispheres of radii 2 cm and 4 cm respectively are melted and recast into another hemisphere. What is the approximate total surface area of the newly formed hemisphere?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the given hemispheres are melted and recast, the total volume remains constant.

R³ = r₁³ + r₂³ ⇒ R³ = 2³ + 4³ = 8 + 64 = 72

Total Surface Area of new hemisphere = 3 × π × R²

TSA = 3 × π × (72)²/³ ≈ 3 × 3.1416 × 17.307 ≈ 163.11 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 163 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the first hemisphere (r₁) = 2 cm

Radius of the second hemisphere (r₂) = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere = 2/3 × π × r³

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a hemisphere = 3 × π × r²
